key_insight: Agent-RRM is a multi‑faceted reward model that turns sparse outcome signals into structured, step‑level feedback on reasoning trajectories, improving training signals for agentic RL.
problem_solved: Overcomes reliance on sparse outcome-based rewards that fail to distinguish intermediate reasoning quality, which leads to inefficient learning and suboptimal agent behavior.
method: Design Agent-RRM to score agent trajectories along multiple axes (e.g., correctness, coherence, tool-use fidelity, efficiency), producing structured, step-level rewards.
Train the reward model from annotated trajectories and/or model-based evaluators to predict intermediate reasoning quality.
Integrate Agent-RRM into the agentic RL loop to provide dense shaped rewards for policy optimization and targeted fine-tuning.
impact: Provides finer-grained, interpretable training signals that improve sample efficiency, robustness, and diagnosability of reasoning agents—enabling practitioners to train and debug agents more effectively.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agent -> actions/tools -> Agent-RRM scoring each step -> shaped rewards -> policy update
Bar chart: performance/sample-efficiency comparison (sparse reward vs Agent-RRM)
Radar chart: multi-dimensional reward breakdown for a single trajectory (correctness, coherence, tool-use, efficiency)
Annotated example trajectory showing intermediate feedback and how it changes subsequent actions
paper_title: Exploring Reasoning Reward Model for Agents
paper_authors: Kaixuan Fan, Kaituo Feng, Manyuan Zhang, Tianshuo Peng, Zhixun Li
